title: Laya via Unsloth Desktop's Decision API (678 MB, 4 GB RAM)
slug_note: Unsloth serves Laya on a Jev-compatible API; existing Jev code works by changing two environment variables.

variation.quant_detail: Unsloth's default: Laya multilingual, 678 MB, 4 GB RAM minimum, 1024-token context (Unsloth guide)

engine.config: Unsloth Desktop: Settings -> API -> Decision API -> Serve requests

requirements.notes: Unsloth's guide: 4 GB RAM minimum for the 678 MB multilingual default; 5 GB for the 846 MB English or typed-decisions checkpoints.

steps.text: Install Unsloth (see Step 0 in Quick start) and open Unsloth Desktop.
Go to Settings -> API -> Decision API, turn on Serve requests, and confirm the Laya download (678 MB). Your API key is on the same page under Access tokens.

Send requests to http://localhost:8888/v1/systemone with model "laya". To move existing Jev code over, set TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8888 and TYPESAFE_API_KEY to your Unsloth key (Unsloth guide).

caveats: Decision model: it answers typed questions with probabilities on /v1/systemone; it does not chat, so OpenCode and chat UIs cannot use it.
The first request loads the model (10-20 s); later requests take well under a second on most CPUs (Unsloth guide).
Threshold on probabilities, not confidence: Laya computes confidence differently from Jev (Unsloth guide).

Unsloth can also train your own decision model from Qwen3.5/3.8 or Gemma 4 and serve it here; Unsloth has not published its own trained decision checkpoint (none on its Hugging Face page as of 2026-10-13).

sources.note: Unsloth guide: Decision API setup, RAM table, migrating from Jev
